entities.name: Heart Sutra (Prajnaparamitahridaya)
entities.label: Text
entities.summary: The shortest and most widely recited of the Prajnaparamita (Perfection of Wisdom) sutras, comprising only 260 Chinese characters in its standard version or approximately 14 verses in Sanskrit. Despite its brevity, it encapsulates the essence of Mahayana Buddhist philosophy: the bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara declares that "form is emptiness, emptiness is form" (rupa sunyata, sunyata rupa) — all phenomena are empty of inherent existence (svabhava) yet appear interdependently. The Heart Sutra concludes with the mantra "Gate gate paragate parasamgate bodhi svaha" ("Gone, gone, gone beyond, gone completely beyond, awakening, hail!"). It is chanted daily in Buddhist temples across China, Japan, Korea, Tibet, and Vietnam — likely making it the single most frequently recited text in all of Buddhism.
